messages:
elaine: quick sync  i pushed a tiny prototype that publishes fractional 'admission tokens' + per-sku efficiency instead of raw gpu counts. goal: better packing for many small requests and separate cost signal for routing. prototype proto in the doc link: https://redwood.internal/rfc/586

mike: interesting. is the main win network payload or admission semantics?

elaine: packing + semantics. tokens let us treat prewarm as consumable units so short jobs don't waste full slots. also avoids coupling cost_usd directly to capacity. sketch: token snapshot has seq, ttl, sku_factor table, and tenant token balances.

raj: operational worry: eviction today uses discrete slots and tenant priority. fractional tokens could change ordering unexpectedly.

elaine: plan: tokens are advisory for admission and soft-eviction scoring only. hard eviction still consults reserved_slots and active leases. scorer example: eviction_score = base_priority - gamma * capped_token_balance + delta * recent_cost_spike. cap token influence so it can't flip hard SLAs.

sophia: add seq + ttl and a token_staleness metric. if snapshot stale, scorer must ignore tokens and fallback to absolute capacity.

carol: ops/UI note: need clear mapping so SRE understands practical meaning (e.g., 0.05 token ~= one short chat completion). also include per-sku mapping in debug snapshots.

mike: and protect billing: single authoritative cost_source; routing and billing both read the same field.

autoscaler-bot: canary scheduled: headroom-token-econ on canary-3 at 2026-03-23T15:00Z. collect token_staleness, eviction_churn, p95_tail.

elaine: rollout checklist i'll add to RFC: proto w/ seq+ttl, sku_factor, capped scorer, telemetry + dashboards, canary test matrix, rollback if eviction_churn > 3x or p95 > 1.2x baseline. tagging @mike @sophia @raj @carol for review.

mike: :thumbsup: keep hard-SLA shield and small initial canary.

elaine: thanks all, i'll post the RFC follow-up with diffs and a short test plan. closing thread, DM for urgent questions.
